content.title: About
content.content: Cereal Fruit Rings are crunchy dry breakfast pieces made from whole grains and coated with a flavorful fruit glaze. They are ready in seconds – just add milk or yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rings are formed from whole grains such as oats, wheat and rice, preserving most of the dietary fiber.
The fruit glaze usually contains natural fruit juices and a modest amount of sugar.
The product is marketed as a “grab‑and‑go” breakfast and is popular with children and busy adults.
In some markets the rings are sold in single‑serve packets, convenient for school snacks.
Gluten‑free versions exist, using rice and corn starch as the base.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grains provide soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The cereal contains thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: The fruit glaze adds vitamin C and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports stable blood sugar
items.content: Complex carbohydrates release glucose slowly, preventing sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The fruit glaze may contain added sugar, so people with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: Individuals with gluten intolerance or wheat, barley, rye allergies should avoid the product.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: Small rings can pose a choking risk for children under three years old.

items.title: Additive presence
items.content: Some varieties contain artificial flavors and preservatives, which may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place a serving in a bowl, pour milk, kefir or yogurt over it and let it sit for 2–3 minutes. Add fresh berries, nuts or honey for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly to prevent moisture absorption.

infant-formula-enfamil-pregestimil-powde.title: Infant formula, Enfamil Pregestimil, powder, ready to mix with water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Pregestimil is a powdered infant formula designed for newborns and infants with sensitive digestion. It contains pre‑hydrolyzed proteins, easily digestible carbohydrates, and an optimal blend of vitamins and minerals. Preparation is simple: just add clean water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is enriched with pre‑hydrolyzed proteins that are easier for infants to digest.
It includes DHA and ARA – fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
Specifically formulated for babies with heightened sensitivity to regular milk proteins.
Each container provides precise instructions for powder‑to‑water ratio.
Enfamil is a globally recognized brand with over 70 years of experience in infant nutrition.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: Provides a complete set of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals needed for normal infant growth.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Pre‑hydrolyzed proteins reduce digestive workload and help lower the risk of colic.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA aid the formation of neural connections and visual function.

items.title: Stable energy supply
items.content: Balanced carbohydrates provide sustained energy without sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Infants with a confirmed cow‑milk protein allergy may react to this formula; hypoallergenic alternatives should be used.

items.title: Incorrect mixing
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted preparations can lead to dehydration or nutrient deficiencies.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: The powder can absorb moisture; keep it in a dry place and use within the stated period after opening.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Water should be warm (~37 °C); excessively hot water can degrade sensitive nutrients.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder, add clean warm water, and stir thoroughly until smooth. Allow the mixture to cool to body temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the lid tightly sealed and use within 30 days.

content.title: About
content.content: The NFS Nutrition Bar (2889) is a ready‑to‑eat meal replacement bar that provides a balanced mix of protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals. It is designed to support energy levels and recovery after workouts, as well as convenient nutrition when time is limited.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Manufactured under GMP quality standards.
Contains whey protein for fast absorption.
Each serving delivers about 20 g of protein and 5 g of fiber.
Gluten‑free and lactose‑free, suitable for people with intolerances.
Packaging is made from recyclable material.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: High whey protein content promotes muscle protein synthesis after physical activity.

items.title: Provides sustained energy
items.content: Complex carbs and moderate healthy fats deliver lasting satiety and stable energy levels.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: Enriched with B‑vitamins, vitamin D, iron, calcium, and magnesium to support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber and probiotics help maintain regular bowel function.

items.title: Convenient and portable
items.content: Ideal for travel, hiking, and office snacks, requiring no preparation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Whey protein may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Some versions contain added sugars; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Excess protein intake
items.content: Overconsumption of protein‑rich products can strain kidneys in predisposed individuals.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain variants use sucralose or acesulfame‑K, which may be undesirable for some consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is ready to eat straight from the pack. It can be consumed as a standalone snack, blended into a smoothie for extra protein, or used as a quick energy source before training.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 30 days. Discard if any mold odor or off‑flavor develops.

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines lean pork, soft tofu and a variety of vegetables (excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens). It is rich in protein, vitamins and minerals while containing no potatoes or soy‑based sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most affordable sources of complete protein.
Tofu, made from soybeans, provides a plant‑based source of protein and calcium.
Vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini and mushrooms add bright colour and texture.
Excluding carrots and broccoli makes the dish gentler on sensitive stomachs.
Skipping soy sauce reduces the sodium content.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork and tofu together supply all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Tofu is often calcium‑fortified, and pork provides phosphorus – both essential for strong bones.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Pork offers vitamin B12, while the vegetables contribute vitamin B6, aiding nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Colorful vegetables are rich in vitamin C and carotenoids, which combat free radicals.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: The absence of soy sauce makes the dish suitable for those monitoring salt intake.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Pork can contain saturated fats; choose lean cuts and cook with minimal oil.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to soy.

items.title: Digestive load
items.content: Combining meat and tofu can be heavy for some stomachs; serve moderate portions.

items.title: Cooking temperature
items.content: Pork must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side to rice or quinoa. Lightly sauté the vegetables in olive oil, add sliced pork and cubed tofu, and season with herbs and spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Pork and tofu can be frozen separately in freezer bags for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp Garden Salad is a light dish featuring boiled shrimp, fresh lettuce, hard‑boiled eggs, tomatoes and/or carrots, plus other vegetables of choice. No dressing is added, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are high‑protein and low‑calorie, making them ideal for weight‑controlled diets.
Lettuce provides vitamins A, K and folate, supporting skin and eye health.
Eggs contribute not only protein but also choline, essential for brain function.
Tomatoes are a source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp and eggs deliver high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: The large volume of vegetables and minimal fat make the salad suitable for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and beta‑carotene from carrots help combat free radicals.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Shrimp contain omega‑3 fatty acids that can help lower triglyceride levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Eggs and shrimp provide vitamins B12 and B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Shrimp must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella and other bacterial hazards.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If vegetables are not washed properly, they may retain pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled. It can be enjoyed as a standalone meal or as a side dish. For extra flavor, a light squeeze of lemon or a drizzle of olive oil may be added.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, store the components separately to prevent the lettuce from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Soy based sauce is a traditional condiment made by fermenting soybeans, wheat, salt and water. It has a distinctive aroma, salty‑umami flavor and is used to enhance vegetable dishes, salads, marinades and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first soy sauce originated in China more than 2,500 years ago.
There are several types of soy sauce: light (shōyu), dark, sweet and low‑sodium varieties.
Traditional fermentation can take from several months up to several years.
In Japan soy sauce is called "shoyu", in Korea – "jang".
Soy sauce is often used in vegetarian cuisine as a fish or seafood substitute.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Soybeans provide a complete plant protein, which remains in small amounts in the finished sauce.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Fermentation creates phenolic compounds such as isoflavones that have antioxidant activity.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermented foods can promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Soy sauce contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides modest amounts of B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional soy sauce contains 14‑18 % sodium, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy may experience reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some soy sauces are fortified with MSG, which can cause headaches or a tingling sensation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Histamine content
items.content: Fermented products may contain histamine, triggering symptoms in those with histamine intolerance.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add soy sauce to vegetable stir‑fries, marinades, salads, soups and sauces. It can be diluted with water or vinegar for a milder taste and combined with ginger, garlic and sesame oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep it refrigerated where it retains quality for up to 6 months. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight.

content.title: About
content.content: Soy sauce is a dark salty condiment traditionally made by fermenting soybeans, roasted wheat, salt, and water. It has a rich salty taste with a deep umami note. It originated in China and is now used in the cuisines of Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia, and the whole world. The sauce is added to marinades, soups, sauces, and stir-fries and served with sushi.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy sauce originated in China and spread from there to Japan, Korea, and Southeast Asia.
In traditional production, the sauce ferments for months.
Most kinds of soy sauce contain wheat, so they contain gluten.
There are light, dark, Japanese-style, tamari, and sweet soy sauces.
Umami is a taste created in the sauce by amino acids formed during fermentation, including glutamic acid.

items.title: Boosts flavor
items.content: The umami taste lets you add a small amount of sauce in place of a lot of salt.

items.title: Contains amino acids
items.content: During fermentation, soy proteins are broken down into amino acids.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: The sauce contains melanoidins and other compounds with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A spoonful of sauce is low in calories.

items.title: Fermented product
items.content: Fermentation gives the sauce a complex flavor and aroma.

items.title: A lot of salt
items.content: Soy sauce is very salty, and too much salt can raise blood pressure; people with hypertension and heart or kidney disease should limit it.

items.title: Gluten and allergy
items.content: The sauce contains soy and usually wheat, so it is not suitable for people with allergies to these foods or with celiac disease; special gluten-free versions exist.

items.title: Tyramine and histamine
items.content: Fermented sauce is high in tyramine and histamine; people taking MAO inhibitors and those sensitive to them should be careful.

items.title: Quality
items.content: Sauce made by a fast chemical process may contain undesirable by-products, so it is better to choose naturally brewed sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add soy sauce to marinades, soups, sauces, dressings, stir-fries, rice, and noodles, and serve it with sushi and dumplings. Use it by the drop and taste the dish before adding extra salt. To cut down on salt, choose reduced-sodium versions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened bottles in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep the bottle tightly closed and in the refrigerator so the flavor lasts longer. Discard sauce that has mold or smells sour.
